sketches.title: Runway Takeover
sketches.premise: Two airport bosses fight for control of a runway. Each turn, name one airport thing that can control, block, reroute, or shut down the thing currently standing there. The host decides whether your takeover is real—or just luggage pretending to be a weapon.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing thing only by directly controlling, blocking, rerouting, grounding, or shutting it down; dodging, surviving, ignoring it, and using a bigger version of the same thing do not count.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [airport thing], and I [direct action] the [thing before me]." Example: "I am an air-traffic controller, and I ground the airplane."
sketches.first_card: An airplane is cleared for takeoff.

sketches.title: Security Check
sketches.premise: You are trying to get one item through airport security while your opponent keeps adding a rule, danger, or inspection problem. Each move must be a single airport object or role that exposes, removes, contains, or legally clears what stands before it. The host will call bullshit on a disguise that merely slips past the scanner.
sketches.criterion: A move wins only when it directly reveals, removes, contains, disarms, or authorizes the standing problem; hiding, slipping around it, enduring it, or making it larger is a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [airport thing], and I [directly handle] the [thing before me]." Example: "I am an X-ray scanner, and I reveal the knife in the bag."
sketches.first_card: A sealed suitcase sits on the security belt.

sketches.title: Gate Change
sketches.premise: A flight is trying to reach its gate through a chain of airport obstacles. On each turn, name one airport thing that changes, cancels, opens, closes, or redirects the situation in front of it. The host rewards actual airport power and savages decorative nonsense that just stands there looking delayed.
sketches.criterion: A move beats what stands only if it directly changes its route, status, access, or timing; merely waiting, hiding, taking a different path without affecting it, or using a bigger copy fails.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [airport thing], and I [specific change] the [thing before me]." Example: "I am a gate agent, and I send the flight to a new gate."
sketches.first_card: A crowded flight is heading toward Gate 4.

sketches.title: Baggage Brawl
sketches.premise: Lost luggage has become an airport-wide fight. Each move is one airport thing that identifies, opens, sorts, carries, damages, or returns the thing currently in dispute. The host explains the failure with cold precision, because apparently your suitcase strategy died before boarding.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing thing by directly finding, sorting, opening, carrying, stopping, damaging, or returning it; losing track of it, waiting it out, or bringing a larger version of it does not.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [airport thing], and I [direct action] the [thing before me]." Example: "I am a baggage tag, and I send the suitcase to the right city."
sketches.first_card: A black suitcase has vanished among a hundred identical bags.

sketches.title: Terminal Lockdown
sketches.premise: The terminal is escalating from ordinary inconvenience to full emergency. Each turn, name one airport thing that stops, seals, announces, evacuates, or restores the thing before it. The host gives your losing move the kind of clinical postmortem usually reserved for preventable disasters.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing danger or disruption only by directly stopping, sealing, warning about, evacuating from, or restoring it; hiding, merely surviving, or overpowering it with a bigger copy fails.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [airport thing], and I [direct emergency action] the [thing before me]." Example: "I am a fire door, and I seal off the smoke."
sketches.first_card: Smoke is spreading through the terminal.

sketches.title: Boarding Pass Fraud
sketches.premise: Two airport scammers try to defeat the document or identity currently in play. Each turn, name one airport thing that checks, invalidates, replaces, or proves the thing before it. The host will dissect a fake solution and roast the player for bringing confidence to a paperwork fight.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing document or identity only by directly checking, invalidating, replacing, or proving it; disguising it, ignoring it, surviving inspection, or making a more official-looking copy fails.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [airport thing], and I [specific verification action] the [thing before me]." Example: "I am a passport scanner, and I reject the fake passport."
sketches.first_card: A forged boarding pass is presented at the gate.
